svg.title: When I'd swap the order, and when I wouldn't
svg.desc: Quotes, CVs or projects, on Sonnet or Opus: Ask once. Order moved almost nothing here except one payroll quote, and a clearly worse option never won. Two pieces of writing: Ask twice, with the order swapped. If the picks differ, call it a draw and decide yourself. Drafts moved more than anything else I tested. A small, fast model: Swap every time, or use a larger model for this one job. Haiku changed which draft it chose half the time when I swapped them. It says nothing separates them: Believe the sentence and ignore the name. The name was the first-listed option in 143 of 144 replies. The decision really matters: Ask a second model too, and read where they differ. Disagreement tells you it's a judgement call. It doesn't tell you who's right. The reply sounds sure of itself: Don't take that as a sign the pick is steady. None of the 480 replies to close calls mentioned the order, including the ones that changed with it. All of this comes from short options I wrote myself. Long documents are untested, and they're where I'd expect order to matter more.
